name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 15, 2009

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Pro Tem
MacLean at 5:08 p.m., on June 15, 2009 at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on June 10, 2009, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean
  Mayor Ury (arrived at 5:13 p.m.)

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there is a matter that came to his attention this
afternoon regarding the State Budget and their attempt to take a large percentage of the cities gas

City Council Minutes  1  June 15, 2009
 tax monies. The League of California Cities would like to communicate to the State that the
cities are in opposition to this take-away. If the Council wishes to address the matter this
evening, they will need to take two actions: (1) determine that the need to address this item arose
subsequent to the posting of the agenda; and (2) the need to take immediate action stems from
the theory that the State's budget is due today. Mr. Curley asked that the City Council address
this item under City Attorney Reports tonight.

Mayor Ury arrived at 5:13 p.m.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to declare a
need subsequent to the posting of the agenda and declare that there is a need for immediate
action to challenge the constitutionality of any seizure by State government of the City's street
maintenance funds (Gas Tax revenues).

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

CS1. Labor Negotiations -- The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations Are
  the City and City's Unrepresented Employees. The City's Negotiator is Dennis
  Wilberg.

CS2. Conference with City Attorney Concerning One matter of Existing Litigation
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(a). The Litigation is City of Mission
  Viejo v. CUSD, Case No. 00180049; Companion Case, Rancho Santa Margarita v.
  CUSD, Case No. 00207543.

CS3. Conference with Legal Counsel — Initiation of Litigation. Pursuant to Subdivision
  (c) of Government Code Section 54956.9. One Case Under Consideration.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:17 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:08 p.m. with all five Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council provided direction to staff but there was no

City Council Minutes  2  June 15, 2009
 reportable action from Closed Session.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize the Capistrano Valley High School Varsity Boys Swim Team as 2009 CIF
  Southern Section Division I Champions and Coach Steve Yancey as CIF Swim
  Coach of the Year

  Mayor Ury presented Certificates of Commendation to Coach Yancey and Members of
  the CVHS Varsity Boys Swim Team.

P2.  Recognize the Capistrano Valley High School Varsity Boys Baseball Team as 2009
  CIF Southern Section Division I Champions

  Mayor Ury presented Certificates of Commendation to Coach Zamora and members of
  the CVHS Varsity Boys Baseball Team.

RECESS

At the hour of 6:22 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:29
p.m. with all five Council Members present.

P3.  Presentation by El Toro Water District, Moulton Niguel Water District, and Santa
  Margarita Water District Regarding Various Statewide Water Issues and Local
  Water Rate Increases

  The City Council received the presentation from Bob Gumerman, General Manager of
  Moulton Niguel Water District. John Schatz, General Manager of Santa Margarita Water
  District and Bob Hill, General Manager of El Toro Water District were also present.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The following expressed concern with ongoing construction at 26992 La Paja Lane and inquired
about the City issuing neighborhood awareness forms: Christine Saracino, M.V.; Richard
Cordova, M.V.; and Ann Cordova, M.V.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: stated that the City is constantly looking for ways to spend money and he
suggested the City can save by taking money from reserves to pay off debt on the Library Bonds.

City Council Minutes  3  June 15, 2009
 Robert Bennett, M.V.: respectfully requested that the City Council adopt a resolution to condemn
the closure of O'Neill Elementary School, to support the concept of a Charter School, and to
prohibit use on the O'Neill site for anything other than an elementary education.

Vanetta Perisho, M.V.: expressed concern that Saddleback Unified School District is targeting
Mission Viejo and planning additional school closures. She further expressed concern that there
is no crosswalk on Spadra for children walking to De Portola Elementary School.

Item 32 was taken out of order

City Attorney’s Report

32.  O’Neill Elementary School; Request for Direction; City Attorney’s Office and City
  Staff

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  The following spoke in opposition to the reuse of O’Neill Elementary School for a
  recreation office and/or an adult education facility: Mike Westerland, M.V.; Lisa Van
  Winkle, M.V.; and Linda DeFonce, M.V.

  By consensus, the City Council requested that staff follow-up with responses to questions
  and specific requests for information as outlined in the discussion. Items of interest
  include: (1) cost, to the City, of a crossing guard; (2) an outline of potential traffic issues
  with the proposed re-use of O’Neill School; (3) the SVUSD Superintendent’s spending
  limit; (4) the number of Mission Viejo students vs. the number enrolled in SVUSD; (5)
  information on the proposed charter school and why it was rejected; (6) costs associated
  with formation of a charter school; (7) a copy of the code or chapter that allows for reuse
  of a school and whether or not it falls under administrative authority; (8) a history of the
  current location for the SVUSD recreation facility offices; (9) planned reuse for the
  former recreation facility offices; (10) description and/or documents to outline the
  planning process for upcoming boundary discussion. The Council requested timely
  updates and that staff work to keep the parents informed.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 13, 14, 18, 19, 22 and 23 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate
discussion.

City Council Minutes  4  June 15, 2009
 Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

3.  Summary of FY 2008-09 Budget Amendments To Date

  Received and filed.

4.  FY 2008-09 Budget Amendment for Legal Services

  Adopted Resolution 09-17 Amending the FY 2008-09 Budget for Legal Services Costs.

5.  Check Register dated May 22, 2009, in the amount of $1,188,463.30

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Check Register dated May 29, 2009, in the amount of $3,251,508.68

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

7.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for April 2009

  Received and filed.

8.  Community Development Agency Treasurer's Monthly Report for April 2009

  Received and filed.

9.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA)

City Council Minutes  5  June 15, 2009
   Treasurer's Monthly Report for April 2009

  Received and filed.

10.  Mission Viejo Community Facilities District No 92-1 - Annual Special Tax for Fiscal
  Year 2009-10

  Adopted Resolution 09-18 Establishing an Annual Special Tax for Fiscal Year 2009-10
  for Community Facilities District No. 92-1 (Mission Viejo Freeway Center).

11.  Authorization for Continuing Appropriations and Preliminary FY 2008-09
  Carryovers

  (1) Adopted Resolution 09-19 to Authorize Appropriations Commencing July 1, 2009,
  Based on Prior Year Spending Levels, Until Such Time as the 2009-11 Budget is
  Adopted; and (2) Adopted Resolution 09-20 Authorizing, on an Interim Basis, the
  Carryover of FY 2008-09 Year-End Encumbrances and Periodic Adjustments to the FY
  2009-10 Budget to Reflect Encumbered FY 2008-09 Balances Until FY 2008-09
  Spending is Closed.

12.  Schedule a City Council Meeting on July 20, 2009, and Cancel the August 17, 2009,
  City Council Meeting

  Directed the City Clerk to schedule a regular City Council Meeting on July 20, 2009, for
  the purpose of adoption of the 2009-2011 Budget and directed the City Clerk to cancel
  the City Council Meeting of August 17, 2009.

15.  Olympiad Road Pavement Resurfacing, Alicia Parkway to Jeronimo Road (CIP
  202)

  Awarded the construction contract in the amount of $163,163.00 to All American
  Asphalt, Inc. for the subject project.

16.  Purchase of Pool Chemicals for City Facilities

  Awarded a contract for the subject services to Alpha Water Systems, Inc. for the period
  of July 1, 2009, through June 30, 2011, in an amount not to exceed $216,000.00; and (2)
  authorized issuance of a purchase order to Alpha Water Systems, Inc. for the period of
  July 1, 2009, to June 30, 2010, in an amount not to exceed $108,000.00.

City Council Minutes  6  June 15, 2009
 17.  Janitorial and Related Services at the Mission Viejo Animal Shelter, Thomas R.
  Potocki Conference Center, and Corporate Yard Administration Building

  Awarded contract for the subject services to GCS, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2009,
  through June 30, 2011, in an amount not to exceed $44,000.00; and (2) authorized
  issuance of a purchase order to GCS, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2009, to June 30, 2010,
  in an amount not to exceed $22,000.00.

20.  Annual Routine Monthly Landscape and Facility Maintenance Services for
  Contract Area 6

  (1) Approved Sixth Amendment to the existing contract for the subject services to Nieves
  Landscape, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2009, to October 31, 2009, in the amount of
  $126,076.00 and; (2) authorized staff to issue a purchase order in an amount not to
  exceed $126,076.00.

21.  Annual Maintenance Program for the Repair and Reconstruction of Streets,
  Drainage Channels, Storm Drains, Slopes, and Emergency Response.

  (1) Approved Third Amendment to the contract with L.T. Engineering for the period of
  July 1, 2009, through October 31, 2009, in an amount not to exceed $65,000.00; and (2)
  authorized staff to issue a purchase order to L.T. Engineering for the period of July 1,
  2009, through October 31, 2009, in an amount not to exceed $65,000.00.

24.  Citywide Orthophotography

  Awarded the contract in the amount of $33,605.00 to GEOspatial Professional Solutions,
  Inc., for the preparation of new citywide orthophotography.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Council Member Schlicht noted that the June 1, 2009, Minutes reflect a comment that she

City Council Minutes  7  June 15, 2009
   made for the record on page #11 (item 27). She clarified that she meant to say that after
  spending close to $8 million that intersection will have a future service level rating of D-
  D according to the February 6, 2006, PB Report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, seconded by Mayor Ury, to approve the
  Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of June 1, 2009, as presented.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

13.  Records Retention Schedule

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about a policy for the destruction of electronic
  records.

  City Clerk Karen Hamman responded that the Information Technology Department is
  currently working on a policy that addresses retention of electronic data.

  A motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ledesma,
  to adopt Resolution 09-21 Amending the City of Mission Viejo Records Retention
  Schedule.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

14.  Agreement for Professional Services for Housing Rehabilitation Program - Housing
  Rehabilitation Consulting Services

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht indicated that she feels the City can get a better rate for these
  contract services.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to

City Council Minutes  8  June 15, 2009
   approve Agreement with Housing Rehabilitation Consulting Services from July 1, 2009
  to June 30, 2011, in an amount not to exceed $120,000 for Technical Assistance.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

18.  Revision to the City’s Salary Schedule -- Temporary Employee Classification

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: stated that the City is promoting an increase for part-time
  employment from $75 to $100 an hour with justification that it is difficult to find
  qualified individuals to work at $75/hour. He asked the City Council to explain and
  justify to the public this 25% to 33% increase.

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.

  A motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, to approve
  Resolution 09-22 Amending the City’s Salary Schedule and Establishing Salary Ranges
  for Authorized Job Classifications.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

19.  Energy Efficiency and Conservation Block Grant Application

  Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  A motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ledesma,
  to (1) designate the City Manager, as the proper authority, to process the grant application
  and apply for the funds from the Energy Efficiency and Conservation Block Grants; and
  (2) adopt Resolution 09-23 Establishing a Capital Improvement Project for the
  Installation of a Solar Photovoltaic (PV) System at City Hall, and Amending the FY
  2008-09 Budget to Appropriate Funds for the Installation of the System as Part of the
  Energy Efficiency and Conservation Block Grant Program.

City Council Minutes  9  June 15, 2009
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

22.  Street Sweeping Services

  Council Member Ledesma stated that was hoping to continue this for one meeting to hear
  from the vendor, Sunset Properties, on the issues outlined in the staff report.

  A motion was made by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, seconded by Mayor Ury, to (1)
  approve Second Amendment to the contract with Sunset Property Services for the period
  of July 1, 2009, through October 31, 2009, in an amount not to exceed $100,000.00; (2)
  authorize staff to issue a purchase order in an amount not to exceed $100,000.00; and (3)
  direct staff to return with additional information surrounding the issues from staff's
  perspective and a response from Sunset Properties outlining their disagreement with the
  proposed 0% increase.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

23.  FY 2009-10 Law Enforcement Services Agreement and Additional Special
  Enforcement Services Provided by the Orange County Sheriff’s Department

  Public Services Administration Manager Paul Catsimanes presented the staff report.

  A motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, to (1) approve
  the FY 2009-10 Law Enforcement Services Agreement with the County of Orange for an
  amount not to exceed $15,157,403; (2) authorize the City Manager to approve
  reimbursements related to special enforcement services in an amount not to exceed
  $65,000 for FY 2009-10; (3) adopt Resolution 09-24 of $36,260 for Costs Associated
  with Digital Patrol Video System Acquisition; and (4) approve a payment in the amount
  of $153,975 for the City’s share of the acquisition cost of the digital patrol video system.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  10  June 15, 2009
   AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

RECESS

At the hour of 8:54 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 9:08
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

25.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

26.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean presented the report.

27.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Ledesma presented the report.

28.  SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Council Member Kelley announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the TCC.

29.  Roundabout Intersections Committee Report

  Council Member Schlicht stated that the June 1, 2009, City Manager’s Roundabout
  Report was purposefully one-sided and tainted the decision-making process. She feels
  that the report was both defective in content and deceptive in substance. Council
  Member Schlicht stated that Mr. Wilberg violated the public’s trust and he shattered her
  trust in him.

  Mayor Ury disbanded the Roundabout Intersections Committee.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

City Council Minutes  11  June 15, 2009
 City Manager Wilberg drew the Council’s attention to the material he presented this evening on
the "Parkway Gallery" project.

Community Services Supervisors Dru Maurer and Virginia Chavez outlined the Parkway Gallery
project and presented a preview of the art pieces that are planned to be installed on Crown Valley
Parkway.

Items 31 and 30 were taken out of order.

31.  Proposed New Stormwater National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System
  (NPDES) Permit Issued by the San Diego Regional Water Quality Control Board
  (SDRWQCB)

  City Engineer Rich Schlesinger presented the staff report.

  By consensus, the City Council received and filed the report.

30.  Proposed 2009-11 Budget for the City of Mission Viejo

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented the report and highlighted key aspects of the
  proposed budget.

  The City Council Members made comments and asked staff to return at the June 22,
  2009, Budget Workshop with: (1) the Crossing Guards budget and potential reductions;
  (2) an Olympiad Finish Line project estimate; (3) an update on the General Plan Carbon
  Footprint; (4) next steps in the SR 73/241 connector; (5) information on street lighting
  incentives for Energy Efficiency Retrofits and Community Choice Aggregation; (6)
  clarification of the $3.1 million vs. $2.1 million drawdown amounts; (7) alternatives to
  drawing down reserves; (8) an estimated cost and timing for the Marguerite Aquatics
  Center pool decking; and (9) an outline of proposed increases in Human Resources and
  Information Technology programs.

  By consensus, the City Council received the Proposed 2009-11 Budget.

City Attorney’s Reports (Continued)

City Attorney Bill Curley discussed a matter that arose after the posting of the Agenda regarding
the State’s proposal to take local gas taxes to help balance the State budget. The City Council
voted earlier this evening and determined that the need to address this item arose subsequent to
the posting of the agenda and that there is a need to take immediate action. Mr. Curley suggested

City Council Minutes  12  June 15, 2009
 minor amendments to the Resolution and asked the City Council for authority to make those
changes before transmitting the Resolution to the State.

By consensus, the Council directed staff to return with a report outlining where the City budget
could be adjusted for this possible $1.6 million loss of yearly revenue.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to adopt
Resolution 09-25, as amended by the City Attorney, Authorizing the City Attorney to Cooperate
with the League of California Cities, Other Cities and Counties in Litigation Challenging the
Constitutionality of Any Seizure by State Government of the City’s Street maintenance Funds.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS

33.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City
  Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Kelley

34.  Turf Lane Open Space

  A motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, to pursue
  seeking the permission of the interested parties (the Timberline HOA, LAFCO and the
  County) to go in and mow and clean up this area so it can be used by the neighbors.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley and Schlicht
  NOES:  Ledesma, MacLean, and Ury
  ABSENT: None

  By consensus, the City Council directed the City Attorney to (1) pursue the prior
  proposal to Quitclaim the City’s interests to the Timberline HOA, (2) prior to the next

City Council Minutes  13  June 15, 2009
   City Council Meeting, identify who owns the property, and (3) as a last resort, consider
  pursuing a Quiet Title Action so a judge can rule on the property ownership issue. The
  Council Members also requested a cost estimate to fence the property due to safety
  concerns.

Council Member Kelley praised City Staff for the Murray Center 20th Anniversary celebration.
She also complimented City staff on the recent completion of another Community Emergency
Preparedness Academy. She commended the residents who worked hard to get themselves
trained for an emergency and basic first aid, as well as OCFA, Mission Viejo Police Services,
Mission Hospital, Medix Ambulance and the Red Cross. Council Member Kelley announced
that this year’s Relay for Life was a good success and they exceeded their fundraising goal. She
thanked Mayor Pro Tem MacLean and Council Member Council Member Ledesma for
attending. She again congratulated the Capo Valley Cougars swim team and baseball teams and
announced that six of the players on the baseball team were also honored by the City when she
was Mayor in 2005. Council Member Kelley stated that it is an interesting story that these boys,
who have been playing together since T-ball, have grown to enjoy such good success with the
Capo Valley Cougars.

Council Member Ledesma

Asked Mayor Ury to adjourn the meeting in memory of Noah Krom, the son of Irvine’s Mayor
Beth Krom.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht stated that lying disrupts unity by destroying trust. She assured the
public that she wants her word to be true and trustworthy and she apologized if she upset anyone
at the last Council Meeting. She offered a special thank you and hello to Kelly Rudolph and her
classmates and stated that she had a lot of fun this past week. Council Member Schlicht
announced that she had the privilege to attend an Eagle Scout ceremony for Johl Glenn
Awerkamp who is a third generation Eagle Scout and his Grandfather swore him in. She
outlined Johl’s scouting achievements and stated that it was a very uplifting event. Council
Member Schlicht wished all Dads a happy Father’s Day.

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean complimented the City for its partnership with the First Marine
Battalion Headquarters Division. They Marines held a car wash on Saturday to help raise funds
for their families as they are deployed. Mayor Pro Tem MacLean announced that there were

City Council Minutes  14  June 15, 2009
 over 70 Marines who conducted an eco-friendly car wash using very little water. On behalf of
the Marines and the City, Mayor Pro Tem MacLean thanked all the residents who came out to
show their support.

Mayor Ury

Mayor Ury, once again, complimented the Capo Boys Varsity Swimming and Baseball teams for
their CIF Championships. He announced that he too had a chance to attend the Murray Center
20th Anniversary celebration and he really got an idea of the vision that the founders had for this
City. Mayor Ury stated that he hopes we reach that level of achievement in what we leave for
residents using the facility 20 years from today.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 10:38 p.m., there being no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting in memory of Noah Krom, to Monday, June 22, 2009
at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of July 6, 2009

City Council Minutes  15  June 15, 2009
